results.name: Resistance Band Shoulder Adduction
instructions: Attach one end of a resistance band to a sturdy anchor point at a high height. Stand with your left side facing the anchor point, holding the other end of the band with your right hand.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart. Extend your right arm straight out to the side parallel to the floor, palm facing down.
Pull the band towards your body, bringing your right hand close to your hip, keeping your arm straight.
Slowly return your right arm to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the left side.
tips: Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and reduce injury risk.
Exhale as you pull the band across your body and inhale as you return to the starting position.
Use a resistance band that provides enough tension to challenge your muscles without compromising form.
results.description: Resistance Band Shoulder Adduction is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Resistance Band Standing External Rotation
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and place a loop resistance band around your wrists. Keep your elbows bent at 90 degrees and close to your sides, with your forearms parallel to the floor and pointing forward.
Rotate your shoulders outwards by pulling the resistance band apart while keeping your elbows fixed at your sides.
Slowly return your forearms to the starting position with control, maintaining tension in the band.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and reduce shoulder injury risk.
Exhale as you rotate your forearms outward and inhale as you return them to the starting position.
Keep your elbows fixed at your sides to ensure proper form.
results.description: Resistance Band Standing External Rotation is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back.

results.name: Resistance Band Standing Single Arm Shoulder Extension
instructions: Attach one end of a resistance band to a sturdy anchor point at hips height. Stand facing the anchor point and hold the other end of the band in your right hand.
Extend your right arm up, pointing to the anchor point, with your palm facing down.
Pull the band backward, keeping your arm straight, and until it reaches parallel to your side.
Slowly return your arm to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the left arm.
tips: Focus on engaging your shoulder and upper back muscles throughout the movement.
Keep your elbow slightly bent to reduce strain on your joints.
Ensure the resistance band stays taut throughout the exercise.
results.description: Resistance Band Standing Single Arm Shoulder Extension is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps.

results.name: Resistance Band Standing Single Arm Shoulder Flexion
instructions: Attach one end of a resistance band to a sturdy anchor point at hips height. Stand with your back facing the anchor point and hold the other end of the band in your right hand.
Extend your right arm back, pointing to the anchor point, with your palm facing forward.
Pull the band forward, keeping your arm straight, and until it reaches your lower chest height.
Slowly return your arm to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the left arm.
tips: Focus on engaging your shoulder and upper back muscles throughout the movement.
Keep your elbow slightly bent to reduce strain on your joints.
Ensure the resistance band stays taut throughout the exercise.
results.description: Resistance Band Standing Single Arm Shoulder Flexion is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps.

results.name: Ring Dips
instructions: Grip a pair of gymnastic rings and jump into a support position with your arms straight and rings turned out.
Lower your body by bending your elbows until your shoulders are slightly below your elbows.
Keep the rings close to your body.
Press back up to full extension and repeat.
tips: Rings are unstable; master bar dips first.
Keep your shoulders down and back.
results.description: Ring Dips is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Core.

results.name: Running
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, your arms relaxed by your sides, and your core engaged. Maintain an upright posture.
Begin running by taking quick, powerful strides, lifting your knees higher than jogging.
Swing your arms naturally with each step, keeping them bent at a 90-degree angle.
Maintain a steady, comfortable pace and continue running for the desired duration or distance.
tips: Stay hydrated and take breaks, especially during longer runs.
Breathe steadily and rhythmically to maintain oxygen flow during the run.
Focus on maintaining a relaxed posture and avoid tensing your shoulders.
results.description: Running is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Hip Flexors, Core.

results.name: Shadow Boxing
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, one foot slightly in front of the other, and your knees slightly bent. Position your hands in front of your face in a guard position, with your elbows close to your body. Begin throwing punches in the air, alternating between jabs, crosses, hooks, and uppercuts. Use a full range of motion and rotate your hips and shoulders to generate power. Move around as you throw your punches, incorporating footwork to simulate a real boxing match. Step forward, backward, and side to side, keeping light on your feet. Continue shadow boxing for the desired duration, maintaining a steady pace and controlled movements.
tips: Focus on proper form and technique with each punch to maximize effectiveness and prevent injury.
Breathe steadily, exhaling with each punch and inhaling between movements.
Keep your hands up in the guard position to protect your face, even while moving and throwing punches.
Use your lower body to generate power, rotating your hips and pivoting on your feet with each punch.
Maintain a light and agile stance, allowing you to move quickly and fluidly.
results.description: Shadow Boxing is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Chest, Core.

results.name: Shoulder Tap
instructions: Start in a high plank with your hands under your shoulders.
Lift one hand and tap the opposite shoulder.
Place it back down and tap with the other hand.
Keep alternating while your hips stay still.
tips: Widen your feet for more stability.
Squeeze your glutes.
results.description: Shoulder Tap is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Chest.

results.name: Side to Side Punch
instructions: Stand upright with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart and your knees slightly bent. Hold your fists up in front of your face in a guard position.
Rotate your torso to the left as you punch across your body with your right hand, extending your arm fully. Keep your legs and hips stationary.
Quickly return to the starting position, then rotate your torso to the right as you punch across your body with your left hand.
Continue alternating punches from side to side for the desired duration or number of repetitions, maintaining a steady rhythm and controlled movements.
tips: Focus on rotating your torso to generate power in your punches while keeping your legs and hips stationary.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you punch and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
Keep your fists up in a guard position when not punching to simulate a defensive stance.
results.description: Side to Side Punch is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Chest, Core.

results.name: Single Kettlebell Sled Push
instructions: Place a kettlebell on the sled and grip the handles.
Lean forward at about 45 degrees with your arms extended.
Drive the sled forward with short, powerful steps.
Continue for the set distance.
tips: Keep your back flat.
Push through the balls of your feet.
results.description: Single Kettlebell Sled Push is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a sled machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Hamstrings, Shoulders.
